def: Gordon Moore's observation that the number of components on a chip doubles at a regular interval: yearly in his 1965 paper, about every two years after his 1975 revision.
practice: Transistor scaling has slowed and Dennard scaling ended in the mid-2000s, so AI hardware gains lean on specialization, lower precision and packaging; Epoch AI measured ML GPU price-performance doubling about every 2.1 years (2023).
